meaning.zh:
“即兴的” 或 “未经准备的”。

这个短语源自19世纪晚期，当时有人为了方便在袖口上记笔记，于是当需即兴演讲或发言时，可以阅读袖口上的笔记。这一习惯演变为 “off the cuff” 这种表达方式，用来形容即兴、不经准备的行为或讲话。
meaning.en: This phrase originates from the late 19th century when people used to jot down notes on their shirt cuffs to refer to during speeches or impromptu talks. Over time, this habit evolved into the expression "off the cuff," used to describe remarks or actions made spontaneously and without prior preparation.

lines.en: He gave an *off the cuff* speech that impressed everyone.
lines.zh: 他即兴发表的演讲令所有人印象深刻。

lines.en: I often have to answer questions *off the cuff* during meetings.
lines.zh: 我常常在会议中需要即兴回答问题。

lines.en: Her *off the cuff* comments were surprisingly insightful.
lines.zh: 她的即兴评论出乎意料地有深度。
